description: HesabYar Phase 5-6 (۵ح — Unified panel + review queue): the five §11.2 coming-soon reports wired (trial balance, general ledger, balance sheet, P&L, cash flow) + cheque report 7, unified dashboard with six live sections, one review queue for all 10 exception types, cash forecast calendar, first-class manual imports, and the FK-flush hygiene sweep.

acceptanceCriteria: Trial balance: UI report wired to the US-403 backend, with §11.1 freshness metadata (source, source timestamp, generated at, company + period, report + calculation version, freshness indicator, reproducibility metadata) + drill-down to the general ledger
General ledger per account: backend from the Tryton reference report through the AccountingEnginePort (never client-side recompute — §11.1) + UI with account/period/company filters
Balance sheet: backend + UI with prior-period comparison
Income statement (P&L): backend + UI with prior-period comparison + monthly revenue/expense bar chart
Cash flow statement: backend + UI, three sections (operating / investing / financing) + waterfall chart

Cheque report 7 (notes receivable/payable balance — the ۵ث honest coming-soon): wired to the Tryton reference report through the port, with aging buckets (30/60/90/120+) and party/due-date/instrument filters
Every report states its data source + §7.5 chart type; Excel/PDF export carries the applied filters in the header
REST endpoints under the existing reports routes; scope reports:read; tenant/company scoping honored
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: Wire the five §11.2 coming-soon financial reports (trial balance, general ledger, balance sheet, P&L, cash flow) to their backends, plus cheque report 7 from the Tryton reference report.
userStories.notes: Wave A (first — the other stories build on its endpoints). Depends on: US-403 (trial balance backend), US-502 (Tryton modules), US-535 (cheque reports page). Tryton reference reports come through the port — the engine is the only ledger authority (ADR 0002).
userStories.title: Financial reports backend: 5 coming-soon reports + cheque report 7

acceptanceCriteria: Unified dashboard shows all six sections with LIVE data: پولِ امروز، پولِ در راه، نیازمند توجه (review-queue counters), خزانه، هشدارها، ایمپورت‌های دستی
Every KPI carries its period, company and unit, and links to the filtered operational page (§11.3 requirement)

Company-scoped cheque figures (۵ث deferred item): backend list filter so the treasury widgets (cheque exposure, in-clearing aging, due-soon) scope by company; the dashboard and the cheque center honor the company filter; tenant-wide remains the default

Dashboard Playwright spec updated to current constants (the ci-playwright risk note: 153 accounts, 114 postable, FY 2027, 24 open periods, standards nav live) — the spec must assert the NEW dashboard, not the US-302 one
Persian RTL, VibeFarsi components; tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest green, build green
userStories.description: Unified dashboard UI: six live sections with linked KPIs, plus company-scoped treasury figures.
userStories.notes: Wave B. Depends on US-550 (report endpoints) + US-504 (review-queue counters) + US-535 (treasury widgets). Frontend house rules in apps/admin/AGENTS.md apply. The dashboard batch is slow against remote Supabase (~105s measured in ۵ث) — the spec timeouts must stay generous; CI's Tryton is local and fast.
userStories.title: Unified dashboard UI + company-scoped treasury figures

acceptanceCriteria: All 10 review item types (the 9 §7.2 types + sms_delivery_failed from US-544) visible and resolvable in ONE queue with a uniform structure: mapping, settlement_variance, cheque_exception, bank_unmatched, packaging_reorder, installment_overdue, manual_import_review, cashbox_variance, inbox_dead_letter, sms_delivery_failed
Per-type allowed actions + suggested action + Persian reason for every type (full list in phased design §7.2)
Manual replay from DLQ + mapping learning (Suggest → Auto) + full audit of every action taken on an item
Filters: type / severity / amount / age / channel; default sort critical-first, then oldest
REST: the existing 7-path review API extended where a new action needs it; scopes review:read/resolve/file
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: Complete the one review queue: all 10 exception types with per-type actions, suggestions, manual replay, mapping learning, and full audit.
userStories.notes: Wave B. Depends on US-504 (queue skeleton) + every module's exceptions (settlement, cheque, bank, packaging, installments, SMS, inbox). One queue, not three — each flow files its own types into it.
userStories.title: One review queue: all 10 types, actions, replay, learning

acceptanceCriteria: Cash forecast calendar, monthly view: expected INFLOWS (gateway settlement tranches, sales installments, due received cheques, due invoices) and expected OUTFLOWS (due issued cheques, payable installments/suppliers, packaging purchases)
Two separate columns: قطعی (registered contract / cheque / installment) vs پیش‌بینی (expected sales); collateral cheques appear in NEITHER column, ever
30/60/90/120-day cash-flow forecast (§11.2 settlement report) with the §11.1 freshness metadata
Cheque report 12 (monthly match-trend — ۵ث deferred: no stored monthly match history existed): monthly match history is now stored, and the trend chart renders from it
Cheque report 14 (cheque cash forecast) feeds the calendar: received-cheque collections → expected inflow, issued-cheque clearings → expected outflow
REST endpoints + UI at the dashboard cash section and reports ← cash forecast; Persian RTL, Jalali months; tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest green
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: Cash forecast calendar (confirmed vs forecast, 30–120 days) fed by settlement tranches, installments, cheques and payables, plus the monthly match-trend report.
userStories.notes: Wave B. Depends on US-521 (settlement tranches), US-534 (cheque clearing/matching), US-540 (installment schedules), US-515 (packaging purchases). Money is Rial only; amounts are MoneyIRR digits=0.
userStories.title: Cash forecast calendar + monthly match-trend (report 12)

acceptanceCriteria: Import batch cycle in the panel, one flow for every manual import (statement B1 + settlement P2): upload → format / column-mapping detection (mapping savable per source) → validation + dedup → accounting-effect preview (gross, fee, tax, refunds, net, receivable balance after the batch, expected deposit) → review item → approve → the normal pipeline (same validation, mapping, policy gate, tie-out) → batch variance report
A rejected batch is archived with its reason and is re-runnable; nothing is silently dropped

Pipeline consumer for payment.settlement.received (US-523 deferred: the event exists, no consumer) — settlement receipts arriving as events flow through the same tie-out + auto-post rules as file imports
REST endpoints for batches (upload, preview, approve, reject, re-run, list); scopes banking:import + settlement:manage as applicable; draft by default, auto-post explicit opt-in (ADR 0003 decision 1)
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: First-class manual imports: one batch cycle (upload → mapping → preview → approve → pipeline) for statements and settlements, plus the settlement-received event consumer.
userStories.notes: Wave B. Depends on US-514 (statement import), US-523 (settlement import + three-way matching), US-501 (event pipeline + DLQ). No IMAP fetch in scope (still deferred). No browser automation anywhere (ADR 0003).
userStories.title: First-class manual imports + settlement-received consumer

acceptanceCriteria: FK-flush sweep (CI run #6 lesson): audit every repository that adds parent+child rows in one flush without a SQLAlchemy relationship — the bank import repositories are known to survive on hash-order luck; flush parents before children everywhere the pattern is found; the sweep list is documented in docs/ (which repositories were checked, which were fixed)
US-523 deferred: tick-created late_tranche review filing — when a settlement tick creates a late tranche, a settlement_variance review item is filed (never silent)

Playwright: unified-panel spec covering the dashboard six sections, the cash calendar, one import batch flow end-to-end, and one review-queue action per type-group; responsive checks at 360–390px; serial where specs share state
tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest green, build green; ruff + pyright clean
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI
userStories.description: Hygiene: the FK-flush sweep across repositories, the deferred late-tranche review filing, and the unified-panel Playwright spec.
userStories.notes: Wave C (last — needs the US-550–554 UIs + APIs). The FK-flush lesson from CI run #6: SQLAlchemy 2.0.54 does NOT order a flush by bare-FK dependency without a relationship — proven by probe; the installments repository was fixed with explicit flushes, the bank repositories still rely on luck.
userStories.title: Hygiene: FK-flush sweep + late-tranche filing + panel Playwright
